Fix https://github.com/VirtusLab/orca/issues/190 — NoClassDefFoundError for orca/Flow$package$ on case-insensitive filesystems.

Two top-level-definition files in package `orca` compile to `$package` class names that differ only in case:
- `runner/src/main/scala/orca/flow.scala` → `orca/flow$package$.class`
- `flow/src/main/scala/orca/Flow.scala` → `orca/Flow$package$.class`

On a case-insensitive filesystem (macOS APFS), the JVM looking up `orca/Flow$package$.class` can get `flow$package$.class` from the runner classes directory, failing RoleSettingsFlowTest and FlowLifecycleTest.

Fix: rename one of the two files so the generated `$package` class names no longer differ only in case. Pick a name that fits the file's contents. Update any references (docs, AGENTS.md, build files) to the renamed file. Also check that no other pair of files in the same package across modules has the same case-only collision. The PR should reference "Fixes #190".

resultJson.title: Rename Flow.scala to stage.scala to fix case-sensitivity collision
resultJson.body:
Fixes #190

On case-insensitive filesystems (macOS APFS), the JVM can confuse the package classes generated from two files in package `orca` that differ only in case:
- `runner/src/main/scala/orca/flow.scala` → `orca/flow$package$.class`
- `flow/src/main/scala/orca/Flow.scala` → `orca/Flow$package$.class`

This caused NoClassDefFoundError in RoleSettingsFlowTest and FlowLifecycleTest when the JVM loaded the wrong class.

**Fix:** Rename `Flow.scala` to `stage.scala` to eliminate the case-only collision. The new name reflects the file's content — the stage runtime implementation. Updated ADR 0018 to reference the renamed file.
